7861: Nature-focused land development at 201 Cypress Lakes Circle, Cleveland, about an hour from Houston or Beaumont, behind a gated entrance: 2,000 acres with five fishing lakes, 1.2 miles of sandy beach, pools, a splash pad, an equestrian center, trails and a dog park.  Nightly guests get full-hookup 30- or 50-amp RV pads, booked on RoverPass for at least 2 nights and checked in at the sales office; tents, toy haulers, truck campers and pop-ups are not allowed.  The development also sells homes, cabins, lots and RV pads with owner financing. --Claude
7870: Remote high-desert park at 889 Sombrero Peak on Terlingua Ranch, 35 miles north of Terlingua, its owner living on site: pull-through sites of about a quarter acre with electric hookups, for rigs up to 42 ft.  The sites have no water or sewer; there is a drinking-water fill station, a water trailer that delivers, a honey wagon and a dump station.  The last 1.5 miles are a single-lane dirt road with a small dry creek crossing, quiet hours from 9 p.m. to 9 a.m. rule out radios and generators, and the nearest gas is 35 miles away. --Claude
7879: Music RV park on 36 acres at 2850 PR 8335, Woodville, in the Piney Woods near the Big Thicket National Preserve, open year-round: 41 sites with full 30/50-amp hookups for rigs up to 45 ft, most of them pull-throughs.  Guests gather for jam sessions, stage shows and potlucks in a climate-controlled pavilion; there is a laundry, a small RV parts store, propane and a cabin, and the facilities are smoking- and alcohol-free. --Claude
7911: RV park at 5001 NW Stallings Dr. on US-59 in Nacogdoches, close to SFASU and the brick streets of downtown, run by a new team of owners and managers who plan to expand it: full-hookup 30/50-amp sites, pull-throughs among them, with Wi-Fi and a dump station, for nightly and full-time guests.  Its rate is camper-reported, since the park has no web page of its own: RV Life reviewers paid $40 a night in January 2026 and $50 in October 2026. --Claude
7924: Campground and RV resort at 248 Woodsy Hollow, Goodrich, with two fishing ponds: full-hookup 30/50-amp RV sites, pull-throughs among them, and tent sites with water and electric, by the day, week or month.  There is a swimming pool (no lifeguard, open 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.), community restrooms and showers, a laundry, Wi-Fi, a clubhouse and a playground. --Claude
8136: Campground at 31130 US Hwy 64, Cimarron, at the foot of the Rocky Mountains, under new ownership: full-hookup 30/50-amp RV sites, partial sites without sewer and tent sites, among large shade trees and a creek along its edge.  It is open from April to October, with limited services the rest of the year, and has two bathhouses, a laundry room, a camp store, a screened pavilion and a horseshoe pit; the sites are close together, pull-throughs among them, and some guests stay 4-6 months.  Scout groups bound for Philmont get their own rates and shuttles. --Claude
9800: City of Potlatch RV park at 125 6th Street, inside a city park: back-in sites up to 45 ft and pull-throughs up to 56 ft, all with full 30/50-amp hookups, plus dry-camping cabins and first-come tent spaces.  There are restrooms and showers, Wi-Fi, a dump station, a playground, a clubhouse and grills; the camp host keeps hours from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m., and stays over 14 nights are booked by calling the host. --Claude
10188: Privately owned RV park at 715 N Main St, Tooele, with extra-large full-hookup 30/50-amp pads, back-in and pull-through, for daily, weekly and monthly guests; long-term residents live on site.  It has restrooms, showers, a laundry, a dump station, drinking water, a general store and Wi-Fi.  Its RoverPass listing sold RV sites only by the month ($900) when read on 2026-10-14. --Claude
10478: Port of South Whidbey campground at the Whidbey Island Fairgrounds, 819 Camano Avenue, Langley, the only public campground on South Whidbey and a walk from downtown: 20 RV sites with water and 20/30-amp power, seven of them premium sites along the front that add 50 amps, and a tent area.  Sites are reserved or claimed on arrival and paid online only, for up to 14 days within 30; it is open year-round except during the Whidbey Island Fair, and water hookups are limited from November to March.  There are bathrooms with private showers and a dump station, and campfires must be propane. --Claude
11267: Privately run RV park and campground at 462 Bush Street, Pioche, open year-round: back-in and pull-through sites with full 50-amp hookups, and tent camping.  There are community restrooms and showers, drinking water, a dump station, a laundry and Wi-Fi, and the Million Dollar Courthouse and Boot Hill Cemetery are nearby; quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 8 a.m. --Claude
11276: RV park at 400 East Highway 95 North, Beatty, a gateway to Death Valley National Park: pull-through full-hookup 30-amp sites, up to 60 ft.  There are showers, a laundry, a propane refilling station and fiber-optic internet, and passersby can use the dump station or the water refill station for $5. --Claude
11572: RV-only park at 465 N Maple Street, Colorado City, about an hour's drive from Zion National Park, for short and long stays: every site has full hookups with 30/50-amp electric, and the short-term sites are 50-ft pull-throughs.  There are restrooms and showers, a laundry and fiber internet, and Alfredo A's Mexican restaurant sits in the park's parking lot. --Claude
12653: Campground and marina on the Lavase River in North Bay, 5 km from downtown and 2 km by river from Lake Nipissing, shared with a 23-pad year-round mobile-home community for people 55 and over, more than 40 seasonal sites, cottages and boat slips.  The park's map shows 15 RV sites with water and electric, mostly 30-amp, and 4 basic tent sites; it is open May 15 to October 15.  There is a heated pool, a laundry, free Wi-Fi, washrooms with showers, a dump station, a boat ramp and canoe and kayak rentals; generators are not allowed. --Claude
